elements.label: Figure ES.1
elements.title: Basic Education Output versus Higher Education Output for Selected Countries
elements.content:
Chart type: Scatter plot with trend line
X-axis title: Learning-Adjusted Schooling Years (years, scale 8 to 13)
Y-axis title: Gross Graduattion Ratio at Higher Education, % (%, scale 0 to 70)
Legend: None (individual points labeled by country/economy)

Data points:
- IDN: (Learning-Adjusted Schooling Years ≈ 8.0, Gross Graduation Ratio ≈ 21%)
- PHIL: (Learning-Adjusted Schooling Years ≈ 8.4, Gross Graduation Ratio ≈ 28%)
- THAI: (Learning-Adjusted Schooling Years ≈ 8.7, Gross Graduation Ratio ≈ 25%)
- MEX: (Learning-Adjusted Schooling Years ≈ 8.9, Gross Graduation Ratio ≈ 31%)
- MAL: (Learning-Adjusted Schooling Years ≈ 9.4, Gross Graduation Ratio ≈ 31%)
- CHINA: (Learning-Adjusted Schooling Years ≈ 9.8, Gross Graduation Ratio ≈ 34%)
- VNM: (Learning-Adjusted Schooling Years ≈ 10.4, Gross Graduation Ratio ≈ 19%)
- SPAIN: (Learning-Adjusted Schooling Years ≈ 11.2, Gross Graduation Ratio ≈ 44%)
- US: (Learning-Adjusted Schooling Years ≈ 11.4, Gross Graduation Ratio ≈ 54%)
- POL: (Learning-Adjusted Schooling Years ≈ 11.6, Gross Graduation Ratio ≈ 54%)
- FRAN: (Learning-Adjusted Schooling Years ≈ 11.7, Gross Graduation Ratio ≈ 46%)
- UK: (Learning-Adjusted Schooling Years ≈ 11.8, Gross Graduation Ratio ≈ 54%)
- NLD: (Learning-Adjusted Schooling Years ≈ 12.0, Gross Graduation Ratio ≈ 51%)
- FIN: (Learning-Adjusted Schooling Years ≈ 12.4, Gross Graduation Ratio ≈ 58%)
- KOR: (Learning-Adjusted Schooling Years ≈ 12.5, Gross Graduation Ratio ≈ 56%)
- SGN: (Learning-Adjusted Schooling Years ≈ 13.0, Gross Graduation Ratio ≈ 58%)

Source: HCI data from World Bank (2018a) and GGR at higher education data from UIS (2017). UIS=UNESCO Institute for Statistics.

Factual comparisons:
- Singapore (SGN) and Finland (FIN) achieve the highest Gross Graduation Ratios at higher education (≈58%), while Vietnam (VNM) has the lowest at ≈19%.
- Singapore (SGN) achieves the highest Learning-Adjusted Schooling Years (≈13.0), whereas Indonesia (IDN) has the lowest (≈8.0).
- Vietnam (VNM) is a noticeable outlier, showing relatively high basic education output (≈10.4 years) but falling substantially below the positive trendline with the lowest tertiary graduation ratio among all countries shown.
